findings.title: A future claim needs a warrant
findings.claim: The focus frames a claim about what is to come as answerable by two possible warrants: access to the unseen, or a covenant taken up with the Most Merciful. Wider echoes make these alternatives a test of warrant, while the surah's own promise from the Most Merciful supplies a positive example of a dependable promise.
findings.mechanism: The focus's looking-into-the-unseen verb and its direct object meet the repeated questions in 52:41 and 53:35 about possessing unseen knowledge, while 27:65 and 72:26–27 locate such knowledge with Allah and preserve chosen disclosure as an exception. The focus's taking verb, relational ʿinda phrase, and covenant object meet 2:80's covenant-or-claim-without-knowledge challenge and 3:76/33:23's examples of fulfilled commitment. In 19:61, the Most Merciful's promise is joined to the unseen and described as fulfilled; these contextual contacts return through the focus's unseen, taking, ʿinda, covenant, and divine-name carriers, changing the question into an audit of evidence for future entitlement.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why neither mere confidence nor a forecast is enough: the first route requires access to knowledge held with God, and the second requires a real, binding commitment. The surah's own promised Garden shows what a reliable divine promise looks like, without certifying that the person in the focus has one.
findings.containment: The question leaves both alternatives open and does not assert that the claimant knows the unseen or possesses a covenant. The wider limits concern independent human access; the supplied disclosure exception remains live. The contextual parallels clarify what would count as a warrant but do not settle the claimant's case.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run finding is trusted and has exact focus branch anchors. Wider connection targets supply exact Arabic but no target morphology or lexical analysis, so their contribution is stated as a bounded contextual inference rather than an unqualified lexical claim.

branch_activations.boundary: The focus questions whether such access exists; it does not say the claimant has it or rule out knowledge disclosed by God.

branch_activations.boundary: The unseen is not made permanently unknowable; the supplied exception for chosen revelation remains part of the reading.

findings.title: Covenant is not lineage
findings.claim: A wider parallel lets the focus's covenant alternative read as a human pledge, distinct from divine parentage: 19:78 asks whether someone took a covenant with the Most Merciful, while 21:26 repeats the title and taking expression in a claim that the Most Merciful took a son, then rejects that attribution.
findings.mechanism: The focus's al-Rahman is the carrier; the supplied 21:26 text independently places that same visible divine title with a sonship claim and its correction. The repeated title and taking surface return through 19:78:6:2 and the focus's taking/covenant relation at 19:78:4:1 and 19:78:7:1, distinguishing a binding human commitment from a claim of divine kinship.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the focus's covenant as an accountable relation with the Most Merciful, while recognizing that a claim of divine descent is a separate relation and is rejected in the wider parallel.
findings.containment: The focus itself does not mention a son or claim kinship. The comparison does not translate al-Rahman as a biological relative or identify the speakers across the two passages.

epistemic.reason: This bounded inference uses the exact focus surface and exact Arabic target in a weak-labeled connection, whose target morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied. Only the repeated title/taking surface and explicit son claim/rebuttal are asserted.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Ortak soydan gelme, kişiler arasında yakın ve kalıcı bir soy ilişkisi kurar.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's divine title al-Rahman is the carrier through which a kinship relation becomes contextually available.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied target at 21:26 pairs al-Rahman with a claim that he took a son and immediately rejects the attribution.
branch_activations.activation: The separate sonship claim supplies a concrete kinship trigger; its return through the focus title and taking/covenant relation makes the focus's human pledge distinguishable from the rejected claim of divine lineage.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's covenant remains a binding human commitment with the Most Merciful, while the wider comparison keeps that relation separate from divine parentage.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus title is not a biological gloss, and the wider correction does not imply that the focus itself raises a sonship claim.
